en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is an active stratovolcano known for its near-perfect, symmetrical cone shape.
The tamaraw is a small, horned buffalo endemic only to the island of Mindoro in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which holds a crater lake, creating a rare lake-within-a-lake-within-a-lake formation.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The waling-waling is a rare, epiphytic orchid species native to the montane forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse marine biodiversity.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippines experiences the amihan, a cool northeast monsoon from November to February, which brings dry weather to most of the country.
The Philippines is one of the world's largest producers of nickel, a metal heavily mined in the provinces of Surigao and Palawan.
The Sierra Madre mountain range runs along the eastern coast of Luzon, protecting the region from strong Pacific typhoons.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
